Ares (formerly Hermes Android) is free and open source. If it is useful to you, you can
 buy me a coffee — entirely optional,
 and it never gates a feature.
 

 

 Watch the 80 second showcase. No voiceover. The score is original synthwave written for this film. It was recorded on the production-signed 4.0.0-rc.7 build during the candidate cycle, with illustrative fixture chats. 4.0.19 is the latest stable release. NextGen adapts the Kyllene design by Giton22 (MIT).

 Ares - formerly Hermes Android v4.0.19

 Hermes Android is now Ares. In 4.0.0 the app is called "Ares - formerly
 Hermes Android", and the launcher label is Ares. 4.0.19 is the latest
 stable release. The package
 com.hermesagent.hermes android and the signing key are unchanged, so the
 update installs over the existing app. It still connects to
 Hermes Agent.

Android client for Hermes Agent — chat with your Hermes sessions from a phone or tablet over local Wi-Fi or a private Tailscale network.

 Screenshots

Emulator captures of production-signed 4.0.0-rc.7 (version code 30432). Classic and NextGen ship in the same app. Each Classic shot uses a different palette. Each NextGen shot uses a different accent. The chats, jobs and insight figures are illustrative fixture data. See capture details. The 3.0.0 gallery stays on disk for history.

 v2.0.0 merges the community Remote Gateway edition contributed by
 @CristianGCiocoi, with review and
 testing from @AI-Guru and
 @grunjol. The merge brings a unified Desktop
 Gateway JSON-RPC transport, per-chat model selection, multi-attachment uploads,
 durable turn recovery, voice dictation, and a comprehensive test suite.
 See CHANGELOG.md for the full list and the
 merge PR thread for
 the community discussion.

 Current release

 4.0.19 (base build 3075 ) is the latest stable release. Its ABI splits are
 30751 , 30752 and 30753 , each above the highest published 4.0.18
split ( 30743 ). The production package and signer are unchanged. Install over
the existing app; do not uninstall or clear app data. 4.0.19 narrows the
chat model pickers to the providers actually configured on the gateway.

 Download Device Version code 
 --- --- --- 
 ARM64 APK Most current Android phones/tablets 30752 
 ARMv7 APK Older 32-bit ARM devices 30751 
 x86 64 APK x86 64 Android devices/emulators 30753 

Release and checksums · 4.0.19 release notes · Full changelog

Debug builds use the separate com.hermesagent.hermes android.dev package and Android debug certificate. Older production APKs have lower version codes; downgrading can require uninstalling and restoring a backup.

 Before updating

- Updating the APK does not install or configure Hermes host software or the optional mobile-push server companion.
- Quiet mode requires completion metadata for each reply. If an older gateway's saved answers are missing in quiet mode, enable Verbose Mode . Saved/live duplicate handover also needs the gateway's optional complete persisted turn receipt and fresh history; older gateways can retain both sources.
- Assets is partial discovery of shared files, not a complete attachment or filesystem catalogue. Classic downloads are limited to 25 MiB per file. NextGen Save and Share stream delivered files up to 1 GiB; previews retain the 25 MiB budget.
- Protect encrypted backups and their passwords. Backups can contain connection secrets and imported client private keys. See the upgrade notes and compatibility limits.

 Updates

Ares does not check for updates and cannot install them. Update through the store you installed it from (Google Play or F-Droid), or download the APK for your device from the GitHub releases page and install it over the existing app. Builds up to 4.0.17 not installed from Google Play checked GitHub Releases on launch and could download and install an update; later versions have no update check, no installer and no Android permission to install packages. A GitHub APK installs over an existing copy only when that copy also came from GitHub releases: other channels may sign with a different key.

The separate Play AAB is built with ARES PLAY BUILD=true and --dart-define=ARES PLAY BUILD=true . Every distribution links the privacy policy and provides an AI-output report action.

 Background notifications: server setup required

Background push requires the paired mobile-push server companion , installed
and enabled separately for the saved connection's Hermes profile. Updating the
Android APK alone does not install it, and the phone's Refresh / retry only
rechecks availability—it cannot install server software.

The server operator must copy server/mobile-push into the profile's plugins,
generate a private VAPID key, authorise the verified dashboard login in the
companion's policy, and enable both the plugin and policy. Current Hermes plugin
enablement prepares its declared Python dependencies through package management.
Activate it in the dashboard and the gateway/turn processes that load its hooks
and sender worker: use supported live activation/reload, or restart affected
processes after draining active work when a new managed generation is selected.
Current host support is limited to the dashboard's launch profile in trusted
in-process mode; secondary-profile hosts cannot forward the required verified
login. Verify both the API and worker are active. Follow the
server installation runbook,
then enable Settings → Background notifications on the phone and grant Android
notification permission. See the phone setup guide.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Prerequisites
  • Android device or emulator (Android 8+).
  • Hermes Agent installed on the host machine.
  • Hermes Gateway API Server reachable from the Android device.
  • API_SERVER_KEY from the Hermes host environment (~/.hermes/.env).
  • Optional: Hermes dashboard reachable for Memory/Cron/Skills/Settings screens.

Hermes Agent docs: https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs

Install the APK

Download the latest APK from this repository's GitHub Releases page.

For most Android phones, install the ARM64 APK:

adb install -r app-arm64-v8a-release.apk

If sideloading directly on Android, enable Install unknown apps for your browser or file manager, then open the downloaded APK.

1. Start the Gateway API Server

The Android chat/session features connect to the Hermes Gateway API Server. It must bind to an address your phone can reach, not only 127.0.0.1.

Use your normal Hermes gateway/API-server startup command and confirm:

  • host/IP is reachable from Android
  • port is usually 8642
  • API_SERVER_KEY is available in ~/.hermes/.env
2. Optional: start the dashboard for drawer features

Memory, Cron Jobs, Skills, and Settings use the Hermes dashboard API (default port 9119).

Configure a dashboard authentication provider before exposing it to your LAN or tailnet. For password login, Hermes uses dashboard.basic_auth.username, a scrypt dashboard.basic_auth.password_hash, the bundled basic auth plugin, and a separate session-signing secret. Follow the current Hermes documentation for setup; keep passwords and signing secrets out of commands, chat and committed files.

Start the configured dashboard:

hermes dashboard --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9119 --no-open

Enter its username/password in the app's Dashboard / Proxy Settings dialog (see Dashboard access). An existing trusted reverse proxy can supply identity instead. A public /api/status response proves reachability, not successful login: validate a protected route after authenticating.

--host 0.0.0.0 is required when connecting from another device. A localhost-only dashboard cannot be reached from Android.

3. Connect the app

  1. Put the Android device and Hermes host on the same Wi-Fi/LAN (or connect via Tailscale — see below).

  2. Find the Hermes host IP:

    # macOS
ipconfig getifaddr en0

# Linux
hostname -I | awk '{print $1}'

  3. Open the Hermes Android app.

  4. Tap + to add a connection.

  5. Enter:

    • Label: any name, e.g. Home
    • Host: the host IP, e.g. 192.168.1.50
    • Port: 8642
    • API Key: API_SERVER_KEY from the Hermes machine

  6. If your deployment is behind a reverse proxy path, expand Custom proxy and dashboard details and set the gateway/dashboard prefixes there. Do not put URL paths in the Host field; the Host field is just the scheme, hostname, and optional port.

  7. Tap the saved connection to browse sessions.

  8. Tap a session to start chatting, or create a new one.

4. Optional: configure dashboard access

The drawer screens (Memory, Cron Jobs, Skills, Settings) talk to the Hermes dashboard, which can run on a different port from the Gateway API Server and may be password-protected. Configure it per connection — either while adding the connection (expand Custom proxy and dashboard details in the Add Connection dialog) or afterwards:

  1. On the connections list, tap the ⋮ menu on a connection → Dashboard / Proxy Settings.
  2. Fill in:
    • Gateway path prefix — optional reverse-proxy path before gateway /api and /v1 routes, e.g. /profile/peter.
    • Dashboard path prefix — optional reverse-proxy path before dashboard /api routes, e.g. /dashboard.
    • Dashboard behind proxy — enable this when the proxy injects dashboard authentication and the app should not fetch a dashboard SPA token or log in with username/password.
    • Dashboard Port — leave blank to use the default (9119 for HTTP, or the same external port for HTTPS deployments), or set an explicit port if your dashboard is exposed elsewhere.
    • Username / Password — the dashboard's password-login credentials. Leave both blank only when a trusted proxy supplies identity or for a local loopback dashboard. --insecure is not a remote-auth bypass.
    • Hermes profile — only when the dashboard is a machine-level one (hermes dashboard / hermes serve without --isolated) that hosts several profiles. Hermes scopes each JSON-RPC call on that socket by a profile field in the request, and falls back to its own default profile when it is missing, so without this field chats can quietly land in the wrong profile. Use the profile name exactly as in hermes profile list, e.g. sol. Leave blank for an isolated per-profile dashboard.
  3. Tap Save. The app validates the settings against the dashboard before storing them.

When credentials are set, the app authenticates via the dashboard's /auth/password-login flow and reuses the returned session cookie — the same mechanism the Hermes desktop client uses.

usage.title: Using the app
usage.html:
Chat screen
  • Send messages: Type in the input field and tap Send. Enter/Return inserts a new line.
  • Streaming responses: Replies arrive through Remote Gateway JSON-RPC or legacy REST/SSE. The chat follows new content while you are at the end; scrolling up lets you read earlier messages.
  • Current work: the responding bar shows the active tool, reasoning or gateway status in either mode. Verbose Mode also exposes retained tool cards, starting collapsed.
  • Verbose mode — Toggle in the app settings. Off shows the conversation only; on exposes retained reasoning, tools, tasks and message metadata in collapsed sections. The bottom status bar shows current work in both modes.
  • Markdown rendering — Assistant messages render markdown (code blocks, tables, lists, links).
  • Message times: local-clock footers follow your device locale and 12/24-hour setting. A tooltip shows the full date and server-recorded versus device-observed provenance. Missing server times are not guessed. Conversation lists retain relative ages.
Inspect a delegated task
  1. Tap a task row in the parent chat's delegated-task card. The app opens Task timeline above the chat, as a phone sheet or a wider-screen dialog.
  2. Expand recorded tool calls for the server's arguments and results, or expand exposed reasoning. Refresh task history checks for saved rows; Load older requests another bounded page. Live previews carry a separate label and do not count as recorded transcript rows.
  3. Close the viewer or press Back to return to the parent's draft and scroll position. The viewer cannot send, steer, stop or watch the child runtime.

Configure authenticated dashboard access for that saved connection first. The API-server key alone cannot read the richer task transcript. Old tasks without a durable child-session reference show Task transcript unavailable. A gateway may omit a newer compression segment or older ancestors; Partial history identifies that gap. Refresh can retry, but reopening does not prove complete history. See Delegated-task timeline for the read-only API, identity checks and backend limits.

Background work and notifications

In the connection's Settings → Background work, use Keep chats active in the background to control device-local connection protection. Turning it off does not stop server work. Use Battery optimisation settings to review Android's restrictions; the app does not request an exemption on startup.

While protection is active, Android requires a foreground-service disclosure. Hermes uses one service for active chats and separate quiet ongoing entries for their status. Settings → Notifications controls optional alerts, including an opt-in report of activity in the open chat and a completion sound. The activity report is off until enabled, counts only input inside the chat (touches, clicks, keys, and typing or focus in the composer), and is sent on the chat's existing connection when the gateway accepts it. Panes that share a connection send one report for the pane used most recently, and leaving the chat withdraws it at once. Pop-out chat windows follow the same setting. The completion sound can be the system sound, Mail, Reminder or silent. Mail and Reminder are original short tones on Android and Apple, desktop sound-theme names on Linux, and Windows notification sounds on Windows. While Ares is open it also plays the chosen sound in the app when a reply finishes (System default plays a short chime); Mute app sounds turns that off. Approvals, other notification kinds, background notifications from the server and Android Auto messages keep the system sound. Returning to the app does not mean all chat notifications should disappear: ongoing work and other chats retain their own state. Grant or revoke OS notification permission in Android settings; the app refreshes that status on return without another startup prompt.

Reopening a stock Gateway chat reattaches to its app-owned turn. After a network drop or process restart, the app reconciles pending markers with saved server history. An acknowledgement or a lost connection does not prove completion; uncertain work remains unresolved and the app does not resubmit its prompt.

For notifications without a live app socket:

  1. The server operator installs/enables the paired server/mobile-push companion and authorises your verified dashboard login. A personal-server owner can be explicitly granted current and future chats with owner_all_sessions: true; restricted accounts keep their restrictions. Installing the APK does not set up the server. Follow Server companion setup.
  2. In the connection's Settings, enable Background notifications and accept Android's notification permission prompt. On Google-enabled phones, the built-in transport needs no separate app, URLs, keys or chat IDs. External UnifiedPush is an optional advanced alternative for Google-free devices.
  3. Keep/reopen Hermes until Active. An encrypted challenge and authenticated confirmation establish registration; Pending does not mean active. Retry after a connection failure. If no supported transport or server is available, the app explains the prerequisite rather than reporting success.
  4. Disable background notifications to revoke consent. Local delivery stops before server revocation; failed remote revocations remain pending for retry.

One installation binds one saved connection. Automatic subscriptions cover only that login's currently authorised durable chats, including future chats allowed by server policy—not other users or profiles. Existing selected-session subscriptions are not silently expanded; disable and enable again to choose automatic scope.

The built-in transport uses Google's network and Play Services, but bundles no Firebase or proprietary Google messaging SDK. Devices without working Play Services need a compatible external distributor. See the dependency licence notice for the upstream licence discrepancy and pre-release review requirement. Push hints and notifications omit chat text; a tap resolves its destination through the authenticated server feed. Push cannot approve an action or resubmit a prompt. See Android UnifiedPush setup and privacy.

Delivery remains best-effort. Force stop, OEM battery controls, Doze, offline devices, distributor availability and notification permissions can prevent or delay it. A foreground service or battery exemption does not guarantee a live connection, and push requires its own working server/distributor setup.

Voice chat

The chat input bar has two voice controls:

Button Icon What it does
Mic 🎤 / 🎤🔴 Tap to start voice dictation. Speak your message — it appears in the input field and sends automatically when you pause. Tap again (or the red stop icon) to cancel.
Voice reply toggle 🔊 / 🔇 Toggles whether Hermes reads its response aloud after a voice-input message. On = 🔊 (volume up), Off = 🔇 (volume off).

How voice replies work:

  1. Tap the mic, speak your question, and wait for the recognition to finish (the text appears and auto-sends).
  2. Hermes streams its response as text in the chat as usual.
  3. After the full response arrives, if the voice reply toggle is on (🔊), the app reads the response aloud using text-to-speech.

Voice replies only trigger when you send a message via the mic button. Typed messages produce text responses only.

Setting up text-to-speech (Android)

Spoken replies require Google Text-to-Speech to be installed and configured on your device. The app uses the device's built-in TTS engine — it does not bundle its own voices.

Step-by-step:

  1. Install Google Text-to-Speech — If not already on your device, install from the Play Store: Google Text-to-Speech
  2. Set as default engine — Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-speech output → Preferred engine → Google Text-to-Speech
  3. Download voice data — In the same TTS settings screen, tap the gear icon ⚙️ next to Google Text-to-Speech → Install voice data → select English (Australia) or your preferred English voice → download
  4. Check media volume — TTS uses the media audio stream, not the ringer. Turn up media volume and make sure your phone isn't in silent/vibrate-only mode.
  5. Test TTS — In the TTS settings screen, tap "Play" to hear a test phrase. If you hear it, the app should work.

features.title: Features
features.html:
• Hermes chat on Android — browse sessions, create new chats, and send prompts to your Hermes Agent.
  • Streaming responses: Remote Gateway chat uses JSON-RPC over WebSocket; REST chat uses POST /v1/chat/completions with SSE. Live text, exposed reasoning and tool activity keep their receipt order without changing request history.
  • Messaging-style UI: ten colour palettes, independent dark/light/system appearance, Markdown, local message times and responsive phone/tablet layouts.
  • Hermes branding: the gold/black default remains available alongside nine other full-app palettes. Chat surfaces, controls, code blocks and navigation follow the selected theme.
  • Gateway API integration — sessions and chat run through the Hermes Gateway API Server, normally on port 8642, with HTTP and HTTPS endpoints supported. Reverse-proxy deployments can set a gateway path prefix that is applied before /api and /v1 routes.
  • Dashboard integrations: Memory, Cron Jobs, Skills, Settings and Remote Gateway chat use the authenticated Hermes dashboard (default port 9119, configurable per connection). Use the built-in password login or a trusted reverse proxy. Current Hermes requires an authentication provider before the dashboard can bind to a non-loopback address; --insecure no longer bypasses this requirement.
  • Model settings — manage the profile default, auxiliary models and ordered fallback providers/models under More → Agent → Model, where the dashboard supports configuration. Chats retain their own overrides. In NextGen this is the Models page, which also shows each model's context window, prices and abilities, and each provider's allowance. See docs/model-management.md.
  • Cron management — list, trigger, pause/resume, create, edit, and delete scheduled Hermes cron jobs.
  • Skills browser — view available Hermes skills with descriptions and trigger conditions.
  • Memory viewer: More → Memory opens saved facts about you from USER.md, with a separate Agent notes tab for MEMORY.md. Reads follow the connection’s Hermes profile; long facts can be read in full. The view is read-only and does not enumerate external providers such as MemPalace. See Saved memory facts.
  • Verbose mode toggle — switch between conversation-only chat and retained reasoning, tools, tasks and metadata, all initially collapsed. Current work remains visible in the bottom status bar in either mode.
  • Task inspection: read recorded delegated-task history without joining or controlling the child runtime. The viewer preserves the parent chat and draft.
  • Background work: keep active stock Gateway turns above chat routes, review device-local battery/notification settings and opt in to separate UnifiedPush.
  • Appearance: Gold, Purple, Orange, Green, Blue, Red, Teal, Pink, Indigo and Cyan, with separate Dark / Light / System controls.
  • Keyboard handling — Enter inserts a new line; use the on-screen Send button to submit. The composer stays editable during setup and replies, so you can draft a follow-up without waiting. A failed submission restores its prompt only if you have not edited the cleared composer. FAB to scroll to bottom.
  • Voice chat — microphone dictation sends recognised speech to Hermes, with optional text-to-speech replies.
